references.text: The earlier procedure for removing infected stones from the house before its complete demolition is described here, showing the progression of measures against leprosy in a house.
The introduction to the laws concerning leprosy in houses, which provides the context for why a house ultimately had to be demolished.
The person with leprosy had to live outside the camp in an unclean place, paralleling how materials from the demolished house had to be brought to an unclean place outside the city.
Unclean persons had to be sent outside the camp, reflecting the principle of removing impurity to a place outside the community.
The command to completely destroy idols and devoted things, parallel to the total destruction of the unclean house.
Jesus prophesies about the temple's destruction, where not one stone will be left upon another, which recalls the complete demolition of the unclean house.
The bodies of the sacrificial animals were burned outside the camp, and Jesus suffered outside the city gate, connecting to the unclean place outside the city.
